newsitem.title: FRANCE: Havas Advertising reshuffle due this wee.
newsitem.headline: Havas Advertising reshuffle due this wee.

text.p: Havas Advertising is to announce this week a rationalisation of its subsidiaries in which it aims to free up 300 million francs and speed up debt repayment, said Alain Cayzac, chairman of Euro RSCG worldwide.

In an interview published in Saturday's edition of Le Figaro newspaper, he said the aim of the reshuffle was to enable the company "to pass from eighth to fifth place in the world before the year 2000".
A spokeswoman at Havas on Monday confirmed that a restructuring was underway.
Havas Advertising, 37 percent owned by Havas, has borrowings of 895 million francs.
In the reshuffle Cayzac would be attached to the holding company of Havas Advertising.
Bob Schmetterer, the French company's advertising associate in New York, would head the international network, which represents two-thirds of Havas Advertising's activity.
A source close to the project said the reshuffle would be "more an evolution than an upheaval".
Cayzac confirmed that Havas Advertising plans to buy an agency in the U.S.
"We have to invest where the business is, that is to prioritise the United States where 50 percent of the world market is located," he told Le Figaro.
"We already make 25 percent of our turnover in the U.S., but on a three-year perspective we want to increase that figure by alliance or through buying (an agency)," he said.
Havas Advertising has been the centre of speculation in the industry following remarks by Havas chairman, Pierre Dauzier, made when Generale des Eaux increased its Havas stake earlier this month.
Dauzier said he would be prepared to reduce Havas's holding in Havas Advertising to 20 percent to allow the unit to pursue its development, particularly on an international scale.
Cayzac said the reshuffle would rationalise the 220 subsidiaries that constitute Havas Advertising.
Over the next three months 10 percent of these would be the object of a recommendation aiming to improve their financial or managerial situation.

"Our aim is to generate a profit of 300 million francs as soon as possible and to get the share price to a level where bond holders would wish to exchange their bonds against shares rather than have their bonds repaid," Cayzac said.
"At that point we would have zero francs of borrowings, a positive cash flow and the possibility of investing strongly," he said.
